headline: Aligning cell-type labels to standardized ontologies and nomenclatures across studies
label: Cell Type Nomenclature Harmonization
summary: Cross-study single-cell and text-mined cell-type labels require consistent normalization to standardized nomenclature and ontology identifiers.
synthesis: The common thread across these items is the reconciliation of cell-type identity across heterogeneous sources. TCellAlign uses a multi-agent LLM framework to map study-specific T-cell labels onto standardized nomenclature, with evidence grounding. Pan-human Azimuth applies a supervised neural network to project single-cell data from diverse human tissues onto one hierarchical annotation typology, with cloud and R interfaces. CellExLink addresses the textual side, recognizing cell-type mentions in biomedical text and normalizing them to Cell Ontology identifiers. What is new is the move from per-study labels to shared typologies operating at organism scale, with explicit grounding in nomenclature. The items do not report downstream biological validation of the mapped labels, and their evaluation scopes are only partially described in the available summaries.
